title: Wire BatchPlan into CompletionWriter.commitBatch or delete the unused sealed hierarchy and its test

evidence.quote: /// [CompletionWriter.commitBatch] receives a [BatchPlan] so it knows which

why: batch_plan.dart's own doc comment asserts CompletionWriter.commitBatch takes a BatchPlan; the real signature takes a raw List<CompletionCommand> and never references BatchPlan anywhere in lib/ — grep confirms the only non-doc-comment usages of BatchPlan/LiveBatchPlan/BulkInTrackPlan/LifetimeOnlyPlan are inside batch_plan_test.dart itself (132 lines exercising a class nothing production calls). The same three-tier classification BatchPlan.classify already encodes is instead re-derived independently via CompletionRepositoryImpl._bulkSourceFor — an Evans-lens 'invariant re-derived instead of enforced once' split that could silently diverge (e.g. a fourth CompletionSource value added later would need updating in two unconnected places). MarkCompletionResult.newMilestoneUnlocks is a related vestige of the same pre-DEC-32 design — it is now hard-coded to `const []` at every call site since the auto-unlock ladder was replaced by the spend economy.
recommendation: Either make CompletionWriter.commitBatch accept a BatchPlan and delete _bulkSourceFor in favor of BatchPlan.classify, or delete batch_plan.dart and batch_plan_test.dart as speculative generality that was superseded before it shipped.
acceptance_criteria: grep for `BatchPlan` in lib/ returns either a real call site inside completion_writer.dart/completion_repository_impl.dart, or zero results (type and test deleted); the doc comment on the class matches what actually calls it.
